# Every tools/fdperf/fdperf.cfg* checked against the hardware selection-counter budgets, and
# every lost line cross-checked against the dumps committed under results/.
#
# Reproduce:
#   scripts/fdperf-cfg-check.py --dumps > results/fdperf-cfg-budgets.txt
#   (budget table: tools/fdperf/a7xx-budgets.json, regenerated by
#    scripts/fdperf-cfg-check.py --update-budgets ../mesa27-src/src/freedreno/registers/adreno/a7xx_perfcntrs.json)
#
# Read it as three answers:
#   * which cfg lines the sampler will not read (slot >= the block's counter budget) - the
#     docs said this about fdperf.cfg in prose; here it is for every cfg in the tree;
#   * whether a lost line was measured by some other cfg, or has no reading in any dump on
#     this machine ("NEVER MEASURED"): those ten names are what tools/fdperf/fdperf.cfg-gaps
#     is written for, and they are what that cfg existed for until it was run on 24.11
#     (journal 43, results/games/re4/gaps37/).  Every one of the ten now resolves to
#     "measured by another cfg: results/games/re4/gaps37/fdperf-raw.txt"; what each reading
#     is worth - dead, aliased, or a rate with no unit - is journal 43's, not this file's;
#   * how far one cfg is from holding everything (last table): the union needs 29 of 12 UCHE
#     selectors and 19 of 6 VPC ones, so the cfgs cannot be merged into one.
#
# Written 23.11, journal 41.1; header corrected 24.11 after journal 43 ran the cfg.
# fdperf cfg against hardware selection-counter budgets
# budgets: tools/fdperf/a7xx-budgets.json (chip A7XX, 28 groups)  rule: slot >= block's num is never read
# cfgs: 17
# dumps scanned: 80, distinct names seen: 237

lines past a budget, all cfgs: 22, 0 of them distinct names that no dump carries (lost in 0 places)

What this does NOT decide: whether a counter that fits the budget means what its
comment says (that is a unit question, see docs/fdperf-a7xx.md and queue 34), and
what fdperf does with a slot left out of a section - the binary is not vendored
here, so a gap is reported as a fact about the file, not about the hardware.
